rows.jp: 尊く、自分さえ保っていてくれるなら。
rows.en: Not as long as they remained precious and true to themselves.

ghs.en: If I can just maintain my most sacred of selves.
ghs.assessment: The reflection concerns people preserving their own noble selves. The English makes Taichi preserve 'my most sacred of selves,' shifting both possessor and construction.

highlights.text: If I can just maintain my most sacred of selves.

rows.jp: 人は人を求めるものだけど。

ghs.en: People are the one thing people seek, however,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that people seek other people. 'People are the one thing people seek' adds exclusivity.

highlights.text: People are the one thing people seek, however,

rows.jp: 自己を相手に仮託したら、おしまいだ。
rows.en: But once you stake your identity on someone else, it’s over.

ghs.en: if the partner is just used a pretext for the self, it's all over.
ghs.assessment: Projecting or entrusting the self onto another person is ruinous. The English instead says that the partner is used as a pretext for the self.

highlights.text: if the partner is just used a pretext for the self, it's all over.

rows.jp: そうなる前に、距離を取るしかないじゃないか。
rows.en: All you can do is pull away before that happens.

ghs.en: But before that happens, wouldn't you inevitably keep your distance?
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that before reaching that point, he has no choice but to keep his distance. The English turns necessity into a generalized rhetorical question addressed to 'you.'

highlights.text: But before that happens, wouldn't you inevitably keep your distance?

rows.jp: 世の中、優しくないから。

ghs.en: Because, in this world, there is no kindness.

rows.jp: そのことを霧は理解しているはずなのに。
rows.en: Kiri of all people should have understood that.

ghs.en: And I know Kiri understands this, but,

rows.jp: この矛盾……わかってるのか、霧。
rows.en: Do you see the contradiction, Kiri?

ghs.en: do you understand this contradiction... Kiri?

rows.jp: 「信じる義理はありませんよね」
rows.en: “I have no obligation to believe you.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "I have no duty to believe you."
She aims the weapon.

rows.jp: この距離なら当たるだろう。
rows.en: At this distance, she would hit me.

ghs.en: At this distance I expect a direct hit.

rows.jp: 霧が練習していた、木との距離と重なる。
rows.en: It matched the distance from which I’d seen her practice against the tree.

ghs.en: This distance and the distance with the tree Kiri practiced with overlap.
ghs.assessment: The distance matches the distance to the tree at which Kiri practiced. 'The distance with the tree ... overlap' is ungrammatical.

highlights.text: This distance and the distance with the tree Kiri practiced with overlap.

ghs.en: She likely won't miss.

rows.jp: 「……俺を殺せば、霧も死ぬことになっちゃうよ？」
rows.en: “...If you kill me, you’ll die too.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...you do realize you'll end up dead too if you kill me?"
Kiri: "I do not care."
She smiles.

rows.jp: 「だって、どっちにしろ世界はもう終わりなんですから」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Because either way the world has already ended."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that the world will end anyway. The English says that it has already ended.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Because either way the world has already ended."

rows.jp: 「君の嫌いな人はいないのに」
rows.en: “None of the people you hate are here.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But the people you hate aren't anymore."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that none of the people Kiri hates are present. 'The people you hate aren't anymore' omits the predicate required to express their absence.

highlights.text: Taichi: "But the people you hate aren't anymore."

rows.jp: 「……いなければいいというものじゃないです」
rows.en: “It isn’t enough for them to be gone.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...this was never about wishing them to be gone."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that their absence alone does not make matters right. The English changes this into a denial that she wished them gone.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...this was never about wishing them to be gone."

rows.jp: 「正しくあってほしかっただけです！」
rows.en: “I only wanted people to do the right thing!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "I only wanted for them to act correctly!"
Kiri: "...even you..."
Taichi: "......"
Pure unmixed murderous intent.

rows.jp: 結晶化し、小さな霧を取り巻く文目(あやめ)となって、彩る。
rows.en: It crystallized into an intricate pattern of color around Kiri’s small frame.

ghs.en: It crystallizes, and becomes a tiny design that surrounds Kiri, coloring her.
ghs.assessment: The crystallized intent becomes a pattern surrounding little Kiri and adorns her. The English makes the design itself tiny rather than Kiri.

highlights.text: It crystallizes, and becomes a tiny design that surrounds Kiri, coloring her.

rows.en: If I died, Kiri would die too.

ghs.en: If I die, Kiri also dies.

rows.en: She knew that and had accepted it.

ghs.en: A resignation to her fate,
identical to Touko's.

rows.jp: それを良いと思ってしまう俺がいる。
rows.en: Part of me found that beautiful.

ghs.en: There is a part of me that thinks that is a very good thing.

rows.en: Yet another part of me yearned for company.

ghs.en: On the other hand, there is also a longing for others.
I want memories,
I want to record them,

rows.en: I wanted to carve them into my heart.

ghs.en: I want to engrave them on my heart.

rows.jp: 思い出さえあれば、その輝かしい宝石さえあれば―――
rows.en: If only I had memories—if only I had those radiant jewels—

ghs.en: If there's even just memories, if there's even just those shining jewels---
ghs.assessment: 'Memories' is plural and requires 'there are,' not 'there's.'

highlights.text: If there's even just memories, if there's even just those shining jewels---

rows.jp: ……俺は、本当に人の気持ちをエサにして生きる怪物かも知れない。
rows.en: ...Maybe I really was a monster who lived by feeding on people’s feelings.

ghs.en: ...I might just be a beast that makes food of people's feelings, I don't know.
ghs.assessment: Taichi may be a monster that feeds on human feelings. 'A beast that makes food of people's feelings' is a literal and unnatural construction.

highlights.text: ...I might just be a beast that makes food of people's feelings, I don't know.

rows.jp: 「死ぬ前に、言い残すことはありますか？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Do you have anything left to say before you die?"

rows.jp: 通告をする霧の手は、哀れなほど震えている。
rows.en: As Kiri pronounced my sentence, her hand trembled pitifully.

ghs.en: On notifying me of that, Kiri's hand shakes, pitifully.
She's frightened.
Murder is frightening.
ghs.assessment: Kiri is afraid of killing a person. 'Murder is frightening' converts her personal fear of committing the act into a general observation.

highlights.text: Murder is frightening.

rows.jp: 精一杯に張りつめた心。
rows.en: Her nerves were stretched as taut as they would go.

ghs.en: The heart is strained with all its might.

rows.jp: その不安と理性の風船を割るには、わずかな刺激で事足りる。
rows.en: The slightest touch would pop that balloon of anxiety and reason.

ghs.en: To burst that balloon of unease and rationality all that is needed is a tiny little stimulus.
Just the tip of the needle.
...there is a way to be saved.

rows.jp: 死んでやろうかとも思う。
rows.en: Part of me wondered if I should let her kill me.

ghs.en: And also the thought, shouldn't you just die you bastard?
ghs.assessment: Taichi considers letting himself die or letting Kiri kill him. The English turns this into a second-person insult telling someone else to die.

highlights.text: And also the thought, shouldn't you just die you bastard?

ghs.en: Hesitation.
